comparator.name: Frisian Language and Culture
comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized target names the Frisian Language and Culture track within the 180-EC BA Nederlandse Talen en Culturen, so the exact target-specific track is reconstructed. The current 2026-2027 programme-specific TER defines the complete pathway for the cohort beginning in September 2026: a fixed 60-EC first year, a fixed 60-EC second year and a 60-EC third year containing a 30-EC minor, a 10-EC faculty-wide choice, a 10-EC thesis and a 10-EC internship. The first-year and third-year faculty-wide choices and the minor remain explicit choice space rather than being filled with invented content. The TER notes that the second- and third-year components for this new cohort will enter OCASYS in 2027-2028 and 2028-2029 respectively.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target explicitly names the Frisian Language and Culture route. The 2026-2027 TER recognizes this as the FTC track within BA Nederlandse Talen en Culturen and defines its separate course pathway, language outcomes, thesis language and field-specific second- and third-year requirements. The exact route is therefore selected independently of UCR fit.

programmes.label: Frisian Language and Culture at University of Groningen

exception.reason: The programme is defined by sustained study through and about Frisian: track-specific language use and variation, Frisian linguistics, historical and modern Frisian literature and language culture, research ateliers in Frisian literature and linguistics, a field internship and an independent thesis normally written in Frisian. UCR offers useful adjacent study in general communication, psycholinguistics, stylistics, literary analysis, media, cultural heritage, history, politics and sociology, but it offers no Frisian-language course and no cumulative sequence in Frisian proficiency, linguistics, literature or regional culture. Its one introductory Dutch course cannot replace that progression. A 24-course UCR response would therefore be a broad language-and-culture programme that omits the target's defining Frisian curriculum, not a defensible closest match.
exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026-2027 TER accounts for exactly 180 EC in the selected Frisian Language and Culture track: 60 EC in Year 1 covering literary analysis, Frisian studies, linguistics, language use and a faculty-wide choice; 60 EC in Year 2 covering language acquisition and methodology, Voices of Frisia, historical and modern literature and language culture, Frisian language variation, research ateliers and research approaches; and 60 EC in Year 3 consisting of a 30-EC minor, a 10-EC faculty-wide course, a 10-EC Frisian thesis and a 10-EC internship. The pathway belongs to the first cohort of the renewed full Frisian bachelor track beginning in September 2026; later-year modules are formally defined although they enter OCASYS only as that cohort progresses.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows with course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and Fall-2026 cohort scheduling. MCCCOMM112 Dutch is the only course whose primary purpose is proficiency in a regional European language, and it is a single introductory 7.5-EC course rather than a continuing sequence. MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning and HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics provide general language analysis; MCCCOMM111, MCCCOMM213 and MCCCOMM311 provide rhetoric and communication; MCCLITR courses provide literary theory and comparative literature; MCCMEDI and MCCHEAM courses provide media and cultural-heritage study; and GOSHIST, GOSPOLI and GOSSOCI courses can address regional history, politics, identity and minority questions. None supplies Frisian proficiency, Frisian phonology and syntax, Frisian language variation, Frisian literary history, field-based Frisian practice or a Frisian-language research sequence. Because these are the programme's organizing core rather than isolated specialist options, the available adjacent courses cannot sustain a defensible 24-course Frisian Language and Culture programme.
